description: The Clawdbot-era macOS app, installed for real, so the predecessor bundle id is a fact rather than a zap-stanza transcription.
why: The macOS app shipped as Clawdis, then Clawdbot, then OpenClaw. This scenario installs the Clawdbot generation so com.clawdbot.mac is proved by a real install like every other identifier. `must_find` names openclaw because the predecessor IS OpenClaw under its earlier name, and the raw probe pins the bundle id itself: must_find alone would pass on any other openclaw route, and this scenario installs none of them.
known_gaps: The bundle id only. com.clawdbot. as a launchd prefix is NOT asserted: the binary contains com.clawdbot.gateway, but a LaunchAgent is registered when the app RUNS and this scenario only installs. Unverified, so not in the catalog either.
Clawdis, the generation before this one, ships its own macOS app and is not covered. Its bundle id has not been read off the artifact, so nothing is claimed about it.
